# Assets

An asset is a file you have uploaded: a screenshot of the product, a team photo, a PDF price list. You upload it once
and use it anywhere.

After reading this guide, you will know:

- How to upload and organise files.
- How one image serves every size the site needs.
- Why alt text belongs on the asset.
- How to check what uses an asset before deleting it.

## 1. The library

**Assets**, in the sidebar, is the library.

![Tidewater's asset library](../../images/cp/assets.png)

- **Upload**, or drag files onto the page. Several at once is fine.
- **Create Folder** to organise them — `product/`, `team/` and `blog/`, say.
- **Search** finds files by name, title and alt text; **Filters** narrow by type.
- Switch between a grid of thumbnails and a list with the buttons at the top right.

What may be uploaded, and how large, is set by the site. If a file is refused, the message says which rule it broke.

## 2. One image, every size

Upload the largest, best version you have. The site never sends that file to a visitor: it asks for a named size —
a card in the blog listing, a wide hero on a landing page, a share image — and Nibble makes each one from your
original, on demand, and keeps it.

**Set a focal point** on an image: the part that must never be cropped out, usually a face or the interesting corner
of a screenshot. Every size keeps it in frame, so the same photo works as a wide banner and as a square card without
uploading it twice.

> [!TIP]
> Changing a focal point or a crop takes effect straight away. The site asks for the new version by a new address,
> so nobody is left looking at a stale image.

## 3. Alt text

Alt text describes an image for people who cannot see it, and for search engines. **It belongs on the asset**, so it
travels with the image to every page that uses it: write it once, and it is right everywhere.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Some fields insist on alt text before they accept an image. It is the single most useful thing you can do for
> someone using a screen reader, and it costs one sentence: "The invoice screen, with the Send reminder button
> highlighted."

## 4. Using an asset

Wherever an entry has an image or file field, choosing it opens this same library — you pick something that exists
rather than uploading another copy. An image placed in rich text is a **reference** to the asset, not a copy.

That is the part worth remembering: **replace the asset, and every page using it follows.** A new logo is one
upload, not a hunt through forty pages.

Video gets a thumbnail generated automatically. Documents and other files work the same way, without the image
tools.

## 5. Before you delete

Each asset shows what uses it. Check that list before deleting.

> [!WARNING]
> If something still uses an asset, deleting it takes the image off that page at once. Deleted assets go to the
> trash like entries, so a mistake can be undone for as long as the trash keeps them.
